title: French for Specific Purposes
source_note: Grounded in standard post-beginner (A1-A2) French grammar (passe compose, futur proche, reflexive verbs, imperative) and functional vocabulary for workplace, travel, and formal communication, building on FRN221's foundational grammar.

questions.question: The 'passe compose' tense in French is generally used to express what?
options: A completed action in the past
A habitual action in the present
questions.correct_answer: A completed action in the past
questions.explanation: The passe compose is a compound past tense used to describe completed actions or events that occurred at a specific point in the past.

questions.question: The passe compose is typically formed using which structure?
options: An auxiliary verb (avoir or être) in the present tense plus a past participle
Only the infinitive form of the verb
The imperfect tense of the main verb
questions.correct_answer: An auxiliary verb (avoir or être) in the present tense plus a past participle
questions.explanation: The passe compose combines a present-tense auxiliary (avoir or être) with the past participle of the main verb, e.g., 'j'ai mangé' (I ate).

questions.question: Which auxiliary verb is used to form the passe compose of most French verbs, including 'manger' (to eat)?
questions.explanation: Most French verbs take 'avoir' as their auxiliary in the passe compose; only a limited set of verbs (mainly motion and reflexive verbs) use 'être'.

questions.question: Which of the following verbs typically takes 'être' rather than 'avoir' as its auxiliary in the passe compose?
questions.explanation: 'Aller' is one of the verbs of motion that takes 'être' as its auxiliary in the passe compose, e.g., 'je suis allé(e)' (I went).

questions.question: What is the correct passe compose form of 'parler' (to speak) for 'j'/'je'?
questions.explanation: The passe compose of 'parler' with 'je' uses 'avoir' plus the past participle 'parlé': j'ai parlé (I spoke).

questions.question: The 'futur proche' (near future) in French is used to express what?
options: An action that is going to happen in the near future
questions.correct_answer: An action that is going to happen in the near future
questions.explanation: The futur proche expresses actions expected to happen soon, similar to English 'going to' constructions.

questions.question: How is the 'futur proche' constructed in French?
options: The verb 'aller' conjugated in the present tense, followed by an infinitive
The verb 'avoir' conjugated in the present tense, followed by a past participle
The imperfect tense of the main verb alone
The conditional form of the main verb alone
questions.correct_answer: The verb 'aller' conjugated in the present tense, followed by an infinitive
questions.explanation: The futur proche uses 'aller' + infinitive, e.g., 'je vais manger' (I am going to eat).

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the 'futur proche' to say 'She is going to travel'?
questions.explanation: 'Elle va voyager' correctly combines the present tense of 'aller' (va) with the infinitive 'voyager' to express near-future action.

questions.question: A reflexive verb in French, such as 'se lever' (to get up), is characterized by what feature?
options: The subject performs an action on itself, requiring a reflexive pronoun matching the subject
It always requires the auxiliary 'avoir' in the passe compose
It cannot be conjugated in the present tense
questions.correct_answer: The subject performs an action on itself, requiring a reflexive pronoun matching the subject
questions.explanation: Reflexive verbs use a reflexive pronoun (me, te, se, nous, vous, se) that agrees with the subject, indicating the action reflects back on the subject.

questions.question: What is the correct present-tense conjugation of 'se lever' (to get up) for 'je'?
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun must agree with the subject: 'je' takes 'me', giving 'je me lève' (I get up).

questions.question: In the passe compose, reflexive verbs are conjugated using which auxiliary verb?
questions.explanation: All reflexive verbs use 'être' as their auxiliary in the passe compose, e.g., 'elle s'est levée' (she got up).

questions.question: The imperative mood in French is used primarily to express what?
options: A hypothetical situation that will never happen
A description of a past event
A formal written business letter's closing
questions.explanation: The imperative mood gives direct commands or instructions, such as 'Écoutez!' (Listen!) or 'Fermez la porte' (Close the door).

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct imperative form of 'parler' (to speak) for the 'vous' form?
questions.explanation: The 'vous' imperative form of regular -er verbs matches the present-tense 'vous' conjugation: parlez (speak).

questions.question: In office/professional French, which phrase would you use to formally request a document by email?
options: Pourriez-vous m'envoyer le document, s'il vous plaît?
questions.correct_answer: Pourriez-vous m'envoyer le document, s'il vous plaît?
questions.explanation: This polite, formal conditional construction ('Could you send me...') is appropriate for professional/business correspondence.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formal way to close a business letter or email in French?
options: Veuillez agréer, Madame/Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées
questions.correct_answer: Veuillez agréer, Madame/Monsieur, l'expression de mes salutations distinguées
questions.explanation: This is a standard formal closing phrase used in French business and administrative correspondence.

questions.question: In a workplace context, what does the French phrase 'une réunion' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Une réunion' means 'a meeting', a common term in French office/business vocabulary.

questions.question: Which French word means 'the manager' or 'the director' in a workplace setting?
questions.explanation: 'Le directeur' means 'the director/manager'; 'le collègue' means colleague and 'le stagiaire' means intern.

questions.question: In French for tourism, which phrase would you use to ask 'Where is the hotel?'
questions.explanation: 'Où est l'hôtel?' directly asks for the location of the hotel, a common tourism-related question.

questions.question: Which French phrase means 'How much does it cost?', useful for shopping or travel?
questions.explanation: 'Combien ça coûte?' is the standard way to ask the price of something in French.

questions.question: Which French preposition correctly completes: 'Je vais ___ Paris' (I am going to Paris)?
questions.explanation: The preposition 'à' is used before names of cities to indicate destination: 'je vais à Paris'.

questions.question: Which French preposition correctly completes: 'Le livre est ___ la table' (The book is on the table)?
questions.explanation: 'Sur' means 'on' and correctly describes the book's position on top of the table.

questions.question: Which French word is used to form the comparative 'more...than', as in 'plus grand que' (bigger than)?
questions.explanation: 'Plus...que' forms the comparative of superiority ('more...than') in French, e.g., 'plus grand que' (bigger than).

questions.question: Which construction is used to form the superlative 'the biggest' in French, as in 'le plus grand'?
questions.explanation: The superlative in French is formed with the definite article plus 'plus' (or 'moins') and the adjective, e.g., 'le plus grand' (the biggest).

questions.question: In an academic context, which French phrase best translates 'I would like to submit my assignment'?
questions.explanation: 'Je voudrais soumettre mon devoir' is a polite, appropriate academic phrase for submitting an assignment.

questions.question: Which French word means 'an exam' in an academic setting?
questions.explanation: 'Un examen' means 'an exam' in French, commonly used in academic vocabulary.

questions.question: When reading a French text for comprehension, what is a recommended first strategy?
options: Skim the text for the general topic and key words before reading in detail
Translate every single word into English before reading further
Read only the very last sentence of the passage
questions.correct_answer: Skim the text for the general topic and key words before reading in detail
questions.explanation: Skimming for gist and recognizing key vocabulary before a close reading is a standard, effective reading comprehension strategy.

questions.question: Which French phrase would be appropriate to formally request an appointment ('un rendez-vous') at the office?
options: Je voudrais prendre un rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît
questions.correct_answer: Je voudrais prendre un rendez-vous, s'il vous plaît
questions.explanation: This polite conditional phrase is the correct, formal way to request an appointment in professional French.

questions.question: Which French word refers to 'a curriculum vitae/resume', commonly used in job application contexts?
questions.explanation: 'Un CV' (curriculum vitae) is the standard French term for a resume, used when applying for jobs.

questions.question: Which French word means 'an invoice', relevant to office and business vocabulary?
questions.explanation: 'Une facture' means 'an invoice', a key term in business/office French vocabulary.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly completes: 'Nous ___ allés au bureau hier' (We went to the office yesterday)?
questions.explanation: 'Aller' takes 'être' as its auxiliary in the passe compose, so 'nous' takes 'sommes': nous sommes allés (we went).
